entities.summary:
Jan Juriewicz Hlebowicz (c. 1480 – April 23, 1549) was a preeminent statesman and military commander of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, whose career spanned the critical transition from the late Medieval to the early modern period in Eastern Europe. As Grand Chancellor of Lithuania (1546-1547) and Palatine of Vilnius (1547-1549), Hlebowicz wielded immense power, shaping the internal administration, judicial system, and foreign policy of a vast multi-ethnic state. His influence was central to the Jagiellonian dynasty's efforts to consolidate power against internal magnate factions and external threats, particularly the burgeoning Tsardom of Muscovy, during a period marked by intense geopolitical competition and the dawn of the Reformation.

Hlebowicz's career was characterized by a steady ascent through the highest offices of the Grand Duchy. He served multiple terms as Voivode of Polotsk (1502–1503, 1506–1516, 1519–1532), a strategically vital borderland province, where he was instrumental in defending Lithuanian territories during the Muscovite-Lithuanian Wars, including the campaigns of 1500-1503 and 1512-1522. His military leadership was critical in skirmishes and sieges, contributing to the defense of Polotsk and other eastern strongholds. Beyond military endeavors, Hlebowicz played a significant role in legal and administrative reforms, overseeing the implementation of statutes that codified Lithuanian law and strengthened central authority.
